title: Illusory promises and constrained discretion
summary: A purported promise raises a consideration problem when its terms leave the promisor no real obligation.
notes: Mattei supplies a good-faith limit on satisfaction; Structural Polymer constrains quantity through good-faith requirements and its price mechanism; Wood finds a reasonable-efforts undertaking in the whole agreement. Interpretation determines whether discretion is actually unbounded. A condition, a termination right, or an unspecified quantity should therefore be analyzed in operation rather than labeled illusory without examining its limits.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 101–117. Open assigned page 101.
